## Mark text by its *importance* {#story .hero-title}

[Use `.key` for the main conclusion.]{.key}

[Use `.aside` for a qualification.]{.aside}

Include inline math, such as $x^2 + y^2 = z^2$, and footnotes in the same text.[^1]

[^1]: This footnote belongs to the first slide.

::: notes
Mark the importance of text in the source. The theme controls its appearance. Presenter notes can also include math, such as $x^2$.[^1]

[^1]: Footnotes in presenter notes have separate IDs from footnotes on slides.
:::

## Keep importance when changing themes {#importance .autoscale}

Compare ordinary body text with `.key` and `.aside` text.

[The central result.]{.key} [A minor qualification.]{.aside}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.key .card}
Add `.key` to a block when the whole block contains the main point.
:::
::: {.aside .callout}
Text fitting shrinks text when a slide would overflow. An `.aside` qualification stays secondary.
:::
::::

Reuse a footnote label on another slide without merging its footnotes.[^1]

[^1]: A different footnote on the second slide.

::: notes
Switch between light and dark modes. The importance of `.key` and `.aside` text stays the same.[^1]

[^1]: A different footnote in the second cue.
:::

## Match code steps to explanations {#code-steps data-step-summary="match"}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {}
```{.python .numberLines data-highlight="4" data-steps="1|2|3" data-step-indices="1|3|7" data-line-matches="1:observations|2:total|3:mean"}
observations = [2, 4, 6]
total = sum(observations)
mean = total / len(observations)
print(mean)
```
:::
::: {}
[Collect the observations.]{.fragment data-match="observations" data-fragment-index="1"}

[Compute their total.]{.fragment data-match="total" data-fragment-index="3"}

[Divide by the number of observations.]{.fragment data-match="mean" data-fragment-index="7"}
:::
::::

::: notes
Use the same names in `data-line-matches` and `data-match` to pair code lines with explanations. The `data-highlight` setting keeps line 4 highlighted during every step. Advance three times to show those pairs. Advance once more for the color-matched overview. Previous restores the last highlight, and earlier explanations remain visible.
:::

## Match equation steps to explanations {#equation-steps data-step-summary="match"}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.equation-steps data-equation-steps="mean|total|count" data-step-indices="1|3|7"}
$$
\htmlClass{mean}{\bar{x}} = \frac{\htmlClass{total}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}}{\htmlClass{count}{n}}
$$
:::
::: {}
[The mean is the quantity we want.]{.fragment data-match="mean" data-fragment-index="1"}

[Add the observations in the numerator.]{.fragment data-match="total" data-fragment-index="3"}

[Divide by the number of observations.]{.fragment data-match="count" data-fragment-index="7"}
:::
::::

::: notes
Give each equation term a class. Here, `mean` marks the mean, `total` marks the sum and `count` marks the number of observations. Use those names in `data-equation-steps` and `data-match` to pair terms with explanations. The fourth advance restores all three terms to full strength. This note also renders $\bar{x}=4$.
:::

## Reveal text one step at a time {#layering}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
[Establish the question.]{.fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

[State the answer.]{.fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
:::
::: {.incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
- Show the evidence.
- Explain the implication.
:::
::::

::: notes
Advance through four reveal frames. Future spans and list items stay hidden. Earlier points dim only because the `.incremental` containers set `data-fragment-effect` to `dim`.
:::
